subject: Urban Planning
title: Berlin Brandenburg Airport: The Terminal That Took 14 Years
description: Learn Berlin Brandenburg Airport: The Terminal That Took 14 Years in one minute.

hook.text: Berlin's new airport was supposed to open in 2011. It finally opened in 2020 — nine years late.

buildup.text: The fire safety system had 170 critical defects. Cables were too short. Escalators ran the wrong direction.

discovery.text: The budget ballooned from 2.8 billion euros to over 7 billion. Three CEOs were fired during construction.

twist.text: The old Tegel Airport, meant to close in 2011, kept running so long that Berliners voted to preserve it.

climax.text: When BER finally opened during a pandemic, passenger traffic was 80 percent below projections.

punchline.text: Germany builds great cars. Airports, not so much.

quiz.question: How many years late did Berlin Brandenburg Airport finally open?
options: It opened two years late in 2013 after minor fire safety fixes
It opened nine years late in 2020 after massive cost overruns and defects
It opened five years late in 2016 after a redesign of the terminal
